messages:
alex: Kicking off GPU burn-up and latency baseline for the new fra1 cluster now. goal: validate driver/kernel pairing, NVLink visibility, and p50/p95 under our steady-state workload.

maria: thanks. what instance type + image?

alex: running on g5x.large-equivalent images (custom ami v2026-02-gpu). kernel 6.1.19, nvidia-driver 535.86, cuda 12.2.

kevin: confirm MIG/partitioning disabled for this run? we want whole-card throughput.

alex: yes — MIG off. full GPU. ops-oncall: can you hold traffic for a 30m soak?

ops-oncall: holding traffic for 40m window starting now. will route low-priority tasks away. :thumbsup:

jyoti: quick checklist I pushed to the node: `modinfo nvidia | grep -E "version|incompat"` then `dmesg | tail -n 60` and `nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/gpu-quant.json`. starting sanity script.

perf-eng: for the benchmark use: 1) seq2seq throughput job (batch sizes 1/8/32), 2) chat-stable p95 traces (prompt length 64/256), 3) small embedding microbench (1k requests @concurrency 64). collect p50/p95/p99 and tail token latency.

alex: running the seq2seq bench now. command: ```bash
./bench-runner --model opt-30b --gpu 0 --batch 8 --seq 256 --iters 2000 --out /tmp/bench-seq.json
```

maria: heard some teams saw a kernel regression with 6.1.19 + 535 driver combo in ams last month — watch for `GPU HANG` / `Xid` messages in `dmesg`.

kevin: checking dmesg on node-07: `Xid 31` only once during boot, then cleared. no persistent hangs. also NVLink shows all peers up. snippet: ```
GPU 0: NVLINK: peer 1 up, link 3/4 active
```

perf-eng: results from first pass (batch=8, seq=256): p50=18ms/token, p95=72ms/token, p99=120ms/token. latency curve looks clean. throughput stable at 310 tokens/sec.

alex: good. logging GPU clocks and power during run: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.gr,clocks.sm,power.draw --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-metrics.csv`. seeing power ~320W sustained.

jyoti: driver module versions: `nvidia 535.86.05`, `nvidia_uvm 535.86.05`. kernel taints: none. thermal throttle: none.

maria: run the embedding microbench next at concurrency 64 and post results. also trigger the routing fallback test: cut primary region for 60s and make sure smart-routing falls back to ded models without error.

ops-oncall: started embedding test. also I triggered a simulated region latency spike via tc: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 200ms`. watch for request timeouts.

perf-eng: embedding microbench p50=4.2ms, p95=14ms, p99=38ms. under network delay test, p95 increased to 220ms as expected but no client errors. under load we saw an allocation stall at 1 minute mark — investigating CUDAMemory allocation latency spike (few events at ~500ms).

kevin: spotted a rare `cudaMalloc` stall in driver logs correlated with one node having a background kernel compile job (persona test). cleaned up that workload. suspect noisy neighbor caused allocation queuing. add to runbook: ensure no non-burnup jobs run on validation nodes.

alex: noted. adding explicit isolation step to bootstrap: tag nodes `infra:validation` and apply nodeSelector in bench job.

maria: cost note — sustained power ~320W at 6 GPUs -> roughly X kWh cost calc per node. add to handoff doc for capacity planning.

perf-eng: final baseline artifacts uploaded to S3: `s3://redwood-validation/fra1/1987654321/`. includes bench outputs, `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and `gpu-metrics.csv`.

alex: ok next: kernel/driver signed-off? any blockers?

jyoti: thumbs up from infra. one small ask: run a kernel variant with 6.1.25 on a sample node to compare p95 (we saw minor jitter). schedule that tomorrow.

maria: I'll follow up with the rollout checklist and handoff doc. thanks everyone. :rocket:

sre-bot: deploy-checklist completed for thread 1987654321 — all required artifacts present.
